title: Pipeline spend ledger row
description: The machine-readable definition of docs/PIPELINE-CONTRACT.md §30. A spend ledger records the model calls that no dispatcher log records, one row per call: the morning job's planner call, the stand-up's turn, the tech lead's turns and the conflict waker's fix sessions (KIT-844, KIT-687). Each caller keeps its own ledger in its own state folder: a JSON Lines file, one row per line, appended by scripts/pipeline_spend_ledger.py's append(). The usage job reads every ledger through the same module's read() and counts the calls beside the dispatcher's logs (§17).
$comment: FIELDS ONLY. Every value is a number, a word from a closed list, a model name that matches a strict pattern, a session id, or a time to the second in UTC. No prompt, reply or error text reaches a row. A figure the CLI did not give is null, never zero: a call whose cost is unknown counts as unpriced. That the row's caller is the ledger's own is checked by the reader, which this schema cannot say.

schema.description: The marker, on every row. The reader leaves a row with any other value out, and says so.

at.description: When the call ended, in UTC to the second. The writer stamps it as it appends the row; a caller cannot.

caller.description: Who made the call: the morning job's planner, the stand-up's turn, a turn of the tech lead's (a DM, or a plan note), or a fix session the conflict waker started. A ledger holds its own caller's rows only.

model.description: The model that carried the call: of the models the CLI's output names, the one it gives the most cost. `other` for a name that is not a plain one. Without such an output, the model the caller asked for, or null when it asked for none.

usd.description: The CLI's own estimate of the call's cost at API prices (`total_cost_usd`), to a millionth of a dollar. Null when the caller could not read it: no JSON output, or an error that gave no total. Never 0 for unknown.

tokens.description: The call's tokens, as the CLI's output reports them in its `usage`. Each is null when the output did not give it.

input.description: `input_tokens`: input not read from or written to the prompt cache.

cache_read.description: `cache_read_input_tokens`: input read from the prompt cache.

cache_write.description: `cache_creation_input_tokens`: input written to the prompt cache.

run_id.description: The CLI's session id for the call, when its output gave one. Null otherwise.

billing.description: How the call was paid for, from the credential the caller handed the CLI. `plan`: a `claude setup-token` token and no key, so the call draws on the plan's usage windows. `key`: an API key, billed by the token. `unknown`: the CLI ran under a sign-in the caller did not choose.
